messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: bessel function order; limited differentiability?
parts:
[moving discussion from stan-users]

On Oct 17, 2015, at 12:56 AM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ...Stan does not implement Bessel functions with real orders for some reason,

Given that Boost has the args templated and explicitly says it'll
handle real inputs, the only problem I'd see to extending those
would be writing the derivatives w.r.t. order.

What we don't have now is a way to say that an argument has
to be data-only and can't be differentiated. So any real valued
argument needs a derivative or there will be parsable Stan
programs that won't compile in C++.

One suggestion (from Daniel, I think) was to implement it, but have
it throw a run-time exception if the argument is a parameter.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] bessel function order; limited differentiability?
parts:
On Saturday, October 17, 2015 at 8:18:05 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
We could --- there's just no way to do it now.  It'd require
a more finely articulated signature (not just shape, but type)
in the symbol table in the function_signatures file.  Then I'd
have enough info to make the checks.

I doubt there is great demand for fixed, non-integer orders to a Bessel function. There are distributions like the GIG

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_inverse_Gaussian_distribution

where it would be ideal if the order could be a parameter, but then we would have to be able to do the differentiation (which involves an infinite sum). If the order is fixed, then it is usually to an integer or sometimes to a half-integer.

Ben
